question: In Table 3, how much lower is the heat generation of the ZrO2 loading with the least heat than that of the bare material, and how much higher is its onset temperature?
rendered:
To calculate the difference in heat generation, we need to subtract the heat generation of the bare material from that of the ZrO2 loading with the least heat (1.5 wt.%). 

Heat generation of bare material: 666.42 J/g
Heat generation of 1.5 wt.% ZrO2: 446.25 J/g
Difference in heat generation: 666.42 - 446.25 = 220.17 J/g

This means that the heat generation of the 1.5 wt.% ZrO2 loading is 220.17 J/g lower than that of the bare material.

To calculate the difference in onset temperature, we need to subtract the onset temperature of the bare material from that of the 1.5 wt.% ZrO2 loading.

Onset temperature of bare material: 231.93 °C
Onset temperature of 1.5 wt.% ZrO2: 245.31 °C
Difference in onset temperature: 245.31 - 231.93 = 13.38 °C

This means that the onset temperature of the 1.5 wt.% ZrO2 loading is 13.38 °C higher than that of the bare material.
